`resetall
`timescale 1ns / 1ps
`default_nettype none

module arbiter #
(
    parameter PORTS = 4,
    parameter ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN = 0,
    parameter ARB_BLOCK = 0,
    parameter ARB_BLOCK_ACK = 1,
    parameter ARB_LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY = 0
)
(
    input  wire                     clk,
    input  wire                     rst,
    input  wire [PORTS-1:0]         request,
    input  wire [PORTS-1:0]         acknowledge,
    output wire [PORTS-1:0]         grant,
    output wire                     grant_valid,
    output wire [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] grant_encoded
);

localparam INDEX_WIDTH = $clog2(PORTS);

reg [PORTS-1:0] grant_reg = 0, grant_next;
reg grant_valid_reg = 0, grant_valid_next;
reg [$clog2(PORTS)-1:0] grant_encoded_reg = 0, grant_encoded_next;
reg [PORTS-1:0] mask_reg = 0, mask_next;

assign grant = grant_reg;
assign grant_valid = grant_valid_reg;
assign grant_encoded = grant_encoded_reg;

wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_request;
assign masked_request = request & mask_reg;

wire request_valid;
wire masked_request_valid;
assign request_valid = |request;
assign masked_request_valid = |masked_request;

// Each bit reports whether a higher-priority request exists.
// These vectors are also the next round-robin masks for their winners.
wire [PORTS-1:0] request_higher;
wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_request_higher;
wire [PORTS-1:0] request_winner;
wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_request_winner;

assign request_winner = request & ~request_higher;
assign masked_request_winner = masked_request & ~masked_request_higher;

genvar p, b;
generate
    for (p = 0; p < PORTS; p = p + 1) begin : priority_bits
        if (ARB_LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin : lsb_priority
            if (p == 0) begin : boundary
                assign request_higher[p] = 1'b0;
                assign masked_request_higher[p] = 1'b0;
            end else begin : interior
                assign request_higher[p] = |request[p-1:0];
                assign masked_request_higher[p] = |masked_request[p-1:0];
            end
        end else begin : msb_priority
            if (p == PORTS-1) begin : boundary
                assign request_higher[p] = 1'b0;
                assign masked_request_higher[p] = 1'b0;
            end else begin : interior
                assign request_higher[p] = |request[PORTS-1:p+1];
                assign masked_request_higher[p] = |masked_request[PORTS-1:p+1];
            end
        end
    end
endgenerate

// Encode the internally generated one-hot winners with parallel OR trees.
wire [INDEX_WIDTH-1:0] request_index;
wire [INDEX_WIDTH-1:0] masked_request_index;
wire [PORTS-1:0] request_encode_terms [INDEX_WIDTH-1:0];
wire [PORTS-1:0] masked_encode_terms [INDEX_WIDTH-1:0];

generate
    for (b = 0; b < INDEX_WIDTH; b = b + 1) begin : encode_bits
        for (p = 0; p < PORTS; p = p + 1) begin : encode_terms
            if ((p >> b) & 1) begin : included
                assign request_encode_terms[b][p] = request_winner[p];
                assign masked_encode_terms[b][p] = masked_request_winner[p];
            end else begin : excluded
                assign request_encode_terms[b][p] = 1'b0;
                assign masked_encode_terms[b][p] = 1'b0;
            end
        end
        assign request_index[b] = |request_encode_terms[b];
        assign masked_request_index[b] = |masked_encode_terms[b];
    end
endgenerate

wire use_masked;
wire [PORTS-1:0] selected_winner;
wire [INDEX_WIDTH-1:0] selected_index;
wire [PORTS-1:0] selected_mask;

assign use_masked = ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN && masked_request_valid;
assign selected_winner = use_masked ? masked_request_winner : request_winner;
assign selected_index = use_masked ? masked_request_index : request_index;
assign selected_mask = use_masked ? masked_request_higher : request_higher;

always @* begin
    grant_next = 0;
    grant_valid_next = 0;
    grant_encoded_next = 0;
    mask_next = mask_reg;

    if (ARB_BLOCK && !ARB_BLOCK_ACK && (|(grant_reg & request))) begin
        grant_next = grant_reg;
        grant_valid_next = grant_valid_reg;
        grant_encoded_next = grant_encoded_reg;
    end else if (ARB_BLOCK && ARB_BLOCK_ACK && grant_valid_reg &&
                 !(|(grant_reg & acknowledge))) begin
        grant_next = grant_reg;
        grant_valid_next = grant_valid_reg;
        grant_encoded_next = grant_encoded_reg;
    end else if (request_valid) begin
        grant_next = selected_winner;
        grant_valid_next = 1'b1;
        grant_encoded_next = selected_index;
        if (ARB_TYPE_ROUND_ROBIN) begin
            mask_next = selected_mask;
        end
    end
end

always @(posedge clk) begin
    grant_reg <= grant_next;
    grant_valid_reg <= grant_valid_next;
    grant_encoded_reg <= grant_encoded_next;
    mask_reg <= mask_next;

    if (rst) begin
        grant_reg <= 0;
        grant_valid_reg <= 0;
        grant_encoded_reg <= 0;
        mask_reg <= 0;
    end
end

endmodule

`resetall
",
  "bottleneck": "The original round-robin feedback path passes masked requests through a priority encoder and then derives mask_next using index arithmetic and a variable shift. The grant path also converts the encoded winner back to one-hot form. These dependent operations are plausible setup-critical paths; no timing report was provided to establish the actual critical endpoint.",
  "rewrite": "Replace the two helper instances with top-local parallel priority reductions. Generate each one-hot winner directly by suppressing requests with higher-priority competitors. Encode these internally one-hot vectors using parallel OR reductions. Compute each candidate round-robin mask directly from the higher-priority-request reductions, independently of the encoded index, then select masked or unmasked results. The frozen helper source is neither changed nor redefined.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The intended gain is removal of the priority-encode-to-index-arithmetic-to-variable-shift chain from the mask feedback path, and removal of binary decoding from the one-hot grant path. Actual setup WNS improvement remains unmeasured and must be established with the fixed EDA settings.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Overlapping priority reductions and parallel encoding may increase logic duplication, routing, or fanout, depending on synthesis sharing. No mapped area result is available. Acceptance requires mapped area at or below 4880.43072 um2, as well as improved setup WNS and equivalence against the frozen original.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Retains the top interface, parameter names/defaults, original register initialization values, single positive-edge clock, synchronous active-high reset, blocking rules, and registered output latency. Arbitrary multi-bit request and acknowledge inputs are supported without one-hot assumptions. For a nonempty priority-selected request set, the higher-priority-presence vector equals the original shifted round-robin mask. The mask holds during blocking and idle cycles. Reset retains priority on every edge, including resets after startup. No startup assumptions, pipeline stages, helper definitions, assertions, or new initialization semantics are introduced. Formal equivalence is still required for the specified PORTS=32 parameter instance."
}
